needs_database.behavior: With a valid non-empty bearer token: 404 'Listing not found' vs 403 'Not authorized' (sellerId mismatch) vs success — all require a real listing/seller row (apps/web/src/app/api/listings/[id]/route.ts:33-34,59-60).
Successful listing of orders filtered by role/status needs real Order rows and relations.
404 'Listing not found', 400 'Listing is not available', and successful order creation (with fee math) all need a real Listing row (orders/route.ts:47-67).
404 'Order not found', 403 'Not authorized', and successful status update need a real Order row (orders/route.ts:84-93).
The grouped-by-Pokemon overview needs real Portfolio/PortfolioItem/Card rows; the empty-portfolio {pokemon:[],...} 200 path also only differs from the error path with real data.

needs_database.route: all /api/portfolios* routes with a valid (non-empty) bearer token
needs_database.behavior: 404 'Portfolio not found'/'Item not found', 403 'Not authorized' (value route), and all successful GET/PUT/POST/DELETE bodies need real Portfolio/PortfolioItem/Card rows owned by the token's userId.
Successful price-point creation (200 {success:true}) needs a writable CardPrice table.

The full success/no-match paths depend on Tesseract OCR output and then a prisma.card search/fallback query; cannot be reached deterministically without DB data (and possibly without network access for Tesseract's language data on first run).
Successful update to isVerifiedSeller needs a writable User row for the token's userId.
available:true vs available:false depends on whether a User with that username exists.
200 with the user object vs 404 'User not found' depends on whether a User row exists for the token's userId.
400 'Username already taken' vs successful update depends on existing User rows.
With a valid (non-empty) bearer token, the paginated/searched user list needs real User rows.
Listing existing items, and 400 'Already in watchlist' vs successful creation, need real WatchlistItem/Card rows for the token's userId.
With a valid (non-empty) bearer token and listingId/ebayItemId present, 404 'Listing not found' vs success needs a real Listing row.

ambiguities_or_bugs.note: Looks like a bug: generateRefreshToken() (apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:31-37) issues a signed JWT, but the refresh handler (apps/web/src/app/api/auth/route.ts:42-61) never calls verifyRefreshToken/jwtVerify — it only base64-decodes the token as 'userId:email' (legacy format) and looks up the first segment as a user id. A real refresh token from this same app would not decode to a valid id string the way the handler expects, so the refresh flow as written only works with hand-crafted legacy tokens, not with tokens the app itself issues. Flagging rather than guessing, since I can't run it against a live DB to confirm the exact failure mode.

apps/web/src/app/api/users/route.ts:8 is the only one of the 32 routes that calls getUserIdFromRequest (apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts), which accepts a real signed JWT (as issued by generateToken) OR the legacy base64 'id:email' format. Every other authenticated route in this list (orders, portfolios*, listings, pokedex, watchlist, seller, ebay, pricing, scan, users/me, users/profile) only does the legacy base64 decode and never verifies a JWT. So a JWT minted by the app's own token issuer would be accepted by GET /api/users but rejected (or silently misread) everywhere else. Possibly intentional inconsistency/leftover from a partial migration — worth confirming with the author.

apps/web/src/app/api/portfolios/[id]/items/route.ts:69 types params as { id: string; itemId: string }, but this file's route segment is only [id]/items — there is no [itemId] folder here, so params.itemId can never actually be populated by Next.js routing. Line 80 falls back to (params as any).itemId after checking searchParams.get('itemId') first, but that fallback looks unreachable/dead. This looks like copy-paste from the itemId-specific route; functionally itemId must be passed as a query string.

Returns HTTP 200 (not 400) with {available:false, error:'Username too short'} for a missing or <3-char 'u' param, unlike most other validation failures in this codebase which use 400. Not necessarily a bug, but worth confirming it's intentional, since a rebuild might reasonably use 400 here instead.

Only checks `authHeader?.startsWith('Bearer ')` (line 16-17) and never decodes/validates the token's contents, unlike the sibling routes in this codebase that reject an empty-token Bearer header (e.g. orders, listings, seller all treat 'Bearer ' with nothing after it as unauthorized). So 'Authorization: Bearer ' alone would pass this route's auth check but fail the equivalent check elsewhere — an inconsistency worth flagging rather than a clear bug.

Uses prisma.portfolio.updateMany({where:{id, userId}, ...}) and always returns {success:true} (line 42-47) regardless of whether any row actually matched/updated — unlike the sibling GET/DELETE handlers in the same file, which return 404/check ownership explicitly. Calling PUT on someone else's (or a nonexistent) portfolio id looks like it would still report success:true. Needs a live DB to confirm, so listed here rather than asserted as a check.
